Subject: Production errors and huge p99 on hosted - urgent

Hi Rachel / Redwood Support,

We started seeing a large jump in p95/p99 latency and a handful of 504s this morning right after our traffic spiked and the hosted autoscaler spun up additional GPU nodes. The spike began ~08:50 PST; we see many first-request latencies in the 8-12s range and a few timeouts. This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of customers.

Attached are a small bundle of traces and a CSV of SLO violations (finpay-traces-20260922.zip, slo-violations-09-22.csv). Sample request IDs: rq_3f7a, rq_3f7b, rq_3f8c.

Can you confirm whether the newly provisioned instances are being prewarmed or if there's a known issue with model load / kernel init on recent runtime? We need a short-term mitigation and an ETA for a fix. We are currently within our renewal window so this is high-priority.

Thanks,

Thanks Rachel. Alicia — I pulled the traces you sent and correlated them with our provisioning logs. Preliminary findings:

- Autoscaler behavior: at 08:47 the pool scaled from 6 -> 9 GPUs. New instances finished VM boot and container startup ~08:49-08:50.
- Model load time: the big model variant FinPay uses (~26B) requires ~6-8s to finish kernel/JIT initialization on those GPUs when no cache present.
- First-request stall: requests routed to freshly started replicas show the classic "cold kernel" pattern — long first-token latencies while kernels compile and pruning/quant ops complete. Subsequent requests from same replica are ~120-200ms.
- Batching interaction: because our routing sent small concurrent requests during the spin-up window, the batcher didn't accumulate enough tokens to amortize the kernel overhead, so the end-to-end p99 increased.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (with low risk):
1) Enable instance prewarm for the FinPay pool (async model preload) — requires a config flip and will warm models on boot path; estimated rollout 5-10 min and should eliminate most first-request stalls.
2) Change traffic policy to route new requests to older warmed replicas for ~60s after spin-ups (temporary sticky routing) — a runtime switch with no code change.
3) As a stop-gap, increase our retry window & soft-client guidance to backoff 500ms x3 for first-request to reduce visible 504s.

I'll start with (1) and (2) after alignment from Rachel/CS. If we apply (1) I'll post follow-up telemetry.

Marcus Lin
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-23T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and huge p99 on hosted - urgent — post-mitigation summary

Quick update following the mitigations we applied late this morning:

What we changed (09:55 - 10:05):
- Flipped the async_prewarm flag for the FinPay hosted pool (model preload on container start).
- Enabled temporary routing policy: new requests for the pool were routed to warmed replicas; new replicas only received traffic after a 45-60s grace window.
- Adjusted autoscaler cooldown from 60s -> 120s for this pool to avoid repeated consecutive spin-ups.

Observed impact:
- Aggregate p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~360ms  within 20 minutes of the config change. p99 reduced from ~8-12s down to ~480-650ms.
- The number of 504s attributable to first-request timeouts dropped to near-zero for flows routed to warmed replicas.
- We captured post-change traces (linked in incident doc) showing kernel/JIT steps happening during prewarm instead of on-request.

Next steps and a medium-term action plan:
- Engineering: add model-level preload safety for large variants and improve warmup telemetry (ETA 3 weeks).
- Product: update runtime default for hosted pools to enable async_prewarm for models above X param threshold (proposal for next week).
- Ops: consider a network-level retry/backoff client guidance for customers; will propose language for our status page.

Alicia — apologies for the disruption. We've left the prewarm + routing policy in place for your pool; if you'd like us to revert any of the changes after a longer observation window, let me know. We'll keep monitoring and I'll send a follow-up in 24 hours with full telemetry.

Evelyn Hart
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
